stem: Rigler's sign is seen on an X-ray when:

options.text: Gas is present on both the mucosal and serosal sides of the bowel wall.
The falciform ligament is outlined by free air.
The stomach is distended and displaces the transverse colon.
Gas is seen branching within the liver parenchyma.

explanation: Rigler's sign occurs in pneumoperitoneum when free air in the cavity outlines the outer (serosal) wall, making the wall itself visible between the internal and external air.
rationale: This sign allows you to see the actual thickness of the bowel wall because there is air inside and outside of it.

optionExplanations.A: Rigler's sign occurs in pneumoperitoneum when free air in the cavity outlines the outer (serosal) wall, making the wall itself visible between the internal and external air.
optionExplanations.B: This describes the football sign, not specifically Rigler's sign, although both indicate free gas.
optionExplanations.C: Gastric distension is a sign of proximal obstruction, not the specific sign of air on both sides of the bowel wall.
optionExplanations.D: Branching gas in the liver is portal venous gas, which is different from free air in the peritoneal cavity.
